1.reason: The float64 reference comparison on line 452 is the independent guard, and the unpreconditioned control reddens it at 6.5e-3 and 7.4e-3. The self-reported asserts are diagnostics.

findings.text: hessenberg is initialised with jnp.eye(width + 1, width) instead of zeros, so any column no Arnoldi step writes keeps a unit diagonal entry; a cycle that exits below width (breakdown at line 1373, or an iteration cap that is not a multiple of the restart width) feeds those junk columns through the QR at lines 1387-1392 and adds a spurious component along a real Krylov vector to the update. Production runs width 20 with max_iterations 400, an exact multiple, so only breakdown reaches it, and test_bank_gmres_zero_right_and_iteration_exhaustion asserts the step count and residual but never the corrupted update.

assert float(step.krylov_condition * step.krylov_residual) <= 1e-8 and the bool(step.converged) assert at line 453 both read values the code itself reports, so they hold whatever the solve actually did; the independent guard is the float64 reference comparison at line 452, and that is the assertion the recorded unpreconditioned control reddens (0.00651 and 0.00744 against 1e-8).

the toy NewtonFactor double still fills the re-typed factor with a dense jnp.eye(size) block_inverse and jnp.zeros(size, jnp.int32) gather indices, which are only shape-correct for a one-cell-per-component toy and are semantically wrong beyond it; it is inert today because step() replaces newton_step and the factor never reaches _block_gmres, but the double no longer carries what the field contract now means.
